newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian bonds drift, seen steady at high levels.
newsitem.headline: Austrian bonds drift, seen steady at high levels.

text.p: 1605 GMT - Austrian bonds drifted sideways on Tuesday, maintaining their current high levels, and traders saw little sign of a decline in the near future.
"We had the first attempts at profit taking but they were very timid," one trader said.
"The mood continues to be friendly, although the air up there is already very thin," said another.

Traders said buyers were waiting for prices to fall but that this looked increasingly less likely. Bonds had received a boost from gains in the U.S. market after yesterday's public holiday, they said.
The market was not expected to be affected by German money supply data due on Wednesday.
* 10 year benchmark 5.875 pct bond maturing July 2006 up 35 bps at 101.15 to yield 5.47 (5.52) pct in bourse trade, quoted post-market at 101.08/101.18 to yield 5.48/47.
* At the near end, five-year 5.50 percent bond maturing March 2001 up five bps at 104.80 to yield 4.26 (4.28) percent in bourse trade, quoted post-market at 104.74/104.84 to yield 4.28/25 percent.
* AGB future up 40 bps at 110.78 on turnover of 260 lots.
* 10-year spread over Germany down one bp at zero, five-year spread up two at one.
* Money market rates stable with three-month VIBOR at 3.300 and overnight money at 2.99/3.24. -- Vienna newsroom, +431 53112 257
